key_insight: DiaCap jointly learns what was said, when it was said, and what the speaker looks like. It treats utterance timing and audiovisual speaker identification as connected tasks rather than separate steps.
problem_solved: Comprehensive dialogue captioning requires aligning speech transcripts with precise utterance times and the correct visually described speakers in a video.
method: Use a single audiovisual large language model to generate a transcript, timestamps, and a visual speaker description for every utterance.
Train initially on 225K curated clips with synthetic captions that densely annotate each utterance.
Apply a second refinement stage; its details are unavailable in the provided, truncated abstract.
impact: Joint modeling could simplify pipelines for speaker-aware video captioning and make dialogue easier to navigate and understand. The provided excerpt does not include evaluation results, so performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Video timeline with color-coded utterances, timestamps, and speaker portraits.

paper_title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
paper_authors: Binfei Ji, Zhiwen Cao, Anqi Yang, Prem Seetharaman, Shuo Yang
